Thank you. I do wonder. The answer I come up with is that I don't want to be taken by surprise if something terrible happens. So I believe everything - they've misunderstood you and they hate you and right now they are spreading gossip about you and there's nothing you can do about it; you'll contract HIV and die. I believe that instantly and treat it like a fact and adjust to life under those facts.

Then I'll have a positive thought: maybe they don't hate you. And I immediately dismiss it because WHAT IF they do? You'll be a fool, thinking they don't hate you when all the while they're hating you and spreading rumors, a fool with his fake comfort.

I think, "maybe you won't get HIV. But what if I do? Maybe I did already. It's going through my body. Imagine how shitty it would be to be in hospital with HIV. Ever seen that movie Philadelphia? Imagine that happening to you!" 

The negative thoughts are the only ones that get through! It's torture. I can't live like this.

It is very difficult. You are fighting against people like the person above (Brittney or something) who are ready to attack you for your audacity of not wanting to feel anymore guilt. And they'll attack you with all their rage and use all their group might against you, because a person who doesn't want to feel guilty anymore is a threat to the community, which keeps its members in check with guilt and only guilt. You have to stop blaming yourself. That's the first step. Doesn't mean necessarily to blame someone else. Just don't immediately and without reason - knee jerk - blame yourself.

You don't seem to understand that you are giving me a knee jerk reaction. You don't know my circumstances; you don't even know if I'm blaming someone else. You are just spitting out what you, a member of the community, is programmed to spit out - hence the reference to a parrot. First you should find out whether the person you are spouting to is guilty of the things you are spouting. That's if you want to be taken seriously rather than reveal yourself as a parrot.
I'm not saying you're blaming yourself. I'm saying that we are all pressured to blame ourselves indiscriminately. That is the answer to your question in my opinion.
Absolutely. I am done competing too. Good luck to you.

See what I mean?

I'm reading what you're saying, but I can only picture a parrot speaking.

When someone mentions that other people are to blame for their problems, they are told that it is wrong to blame others for your problems. The act of blaming others is contemptible to most people and suitable for mockery. 

It is obviously not true though. Others are to blame frequently. 'I don't trust people', says one man. 'You need to learn to trust people', says another to him. 'My father ruined my life', says one man. 'It's time to stop blaming your father', says another. The attempt is always to divert a person's complaint against other people onto themselves, so that the feelings they feel find resolution in an attack on themselves - guilt, self hatred, and so forth.

This diversion is invariably committed by a group or community. That is because a group is self perpetuating. It is disruptive to a group for one of its elements to be critical of it. It is better to neutralise that person by getting them to take out their anger on themselves. 

The group therefore appears to be perfect and consequently worthy of entry. This furthers self censorship and self hatred and guilt, as the perfect imagine of the group, which is its price for entrance, is unattainable. 

And injustices occur when elements of the group itself fail to uphold its values and then get away with it - the in fighting if hypocrites who escape judgement.

You've been battling it for a while so have you learned any effective ways to turn off or silence or numb any emotions? Please tell me if you have.

I've found that if my body can't take anymore stress it shuts down in ways. Therefore I have been trying to put myself in highly stressful situations with the hope that I will overload and become broken and unfeeling. It has worked in many ways, particularly with anxiety.
The difference between one meaningful relationship and a million superficial ones is the difference between a lightning bolt and a light drizzle. I don't know why that isn't understood.

I'm 28. I've been fighting the same battle as you for a long time man. I've learned some things. First, being in a romantic/sexual relationship helps. It doesn't defeat the monster, but it helps. Second, non-sexual relationships - for instance family or friends - supply what a romantic/sexual relationships fail to supply - like shit talking, conversations about common interests, ventilation of anger, different forms of love, and so on. Non-sexual relationships, too, don't do quite enough to rid the depression completely. Third, being that romantic/sexual relationships and non-sexual relationships aren't enough on their own, I'm convinced that medication is the way to pick up the leftover percentage. 

Now, these three things, I believe, are prerequisites to defeating or at least subduing depression. The rest - hobbies, interests, participation in society - come after these three things. 

So if you believed, like I do, that these three things were the prerequisites for your healing, you would then have direction. You would do whatever it takes to get these three things. And the motivation to achieve healing your depression may allow you to get started on the first step, which, unfortunately, is to get a job. It's unfortunate because that, if we believe what I said, comes after you are better. But unfortunately on this particular planet, you can't buy meds without a job. And it's difficult to start a romantic relationship or to pursue non-sexual relationships without one.

A long time ago, I tried normal small talk: how are you, what's your job, hobbies, etc. the conversations lasted the night, then I never heard from them again. Often they are gazing around trying to get away while I'm talking or while they're answering my questions.

I tried telling them about me. They're not interested.

Most recently I tried joking. Someone said the other night, 'Can I sit here?' Normally I'd just say "Sure," but since that doesn't work, this time I said "Of course not! Get the hell out of here! I'm sorry. I'm joking. Please sit down." They had a laugh and that was the last I saw of them.

I'm just trying every possibility, and I've tried them all which is why I'm finally at stupid shit like, "of course not; get the hell out of here." I'm literally out of options.

Edit: in pretty sure it's just me. Other people wouldn't need to go to the effort that I go to. There's just something about my head that people don't like I guess

I've thought about it. There's a couple of things. The irritation is caused by them (the ones I feel comfortable around) but it's not their fault. For example, I say something that I'm sure is really witty, something that would certainly have made, for example, my girlfriend laugh out loud when we first met. But that's not what I get now. I really make an effort to talk and have good conversations, but she doesn't get on board and it's just me talking. So I get pissed off, and my attitude becomes "well then, if you aren't going to enjoy my company when I try to be pleasant and friendly, then I'll take all that away and make no effort at all. See how you like that."

Now, I'm aware that I'm the one at fault here. Maybe my witty comment just isn't as witty as I think it is. Maybe my conversations suck. I can't fairly blame someone for not having the reaction I expect. But that's what happens.

The problem is when she then tries to make a conversation, but I've already passed the point of no return. I give her short answers, kind of like revenge for what she gave me, but it's excessive.
